title: ExtendedAE issue #675: [1.21.1] Smart Annihilation Plane doesn't wake up after its network loses power or channel
licence: GitHub issue thread: user-generated content under the GitHub Terms of Service; the repo licence (LGPL-3.0) does not cover issue text
text:
[issue by Ava2201]
**Environment**
- Minecraft 1.21.1, NeoForge 21.1.250, dedicated server
- AE2 19.2.18
- ExtendedAE 1.21-2.2.35-neoforge (the code in question is unchanged in the current 2.2.38 source)
- Modpack: All the Mods 10 Aeronautics 0.7.0

**Problem**
I use an ME Smart Annihilation Plane (empty filter, no cards) to break certus quartz buds on a budding block surrounded by AE2 Growth Accelerators. After some breaks it stops, a full Certus Quartz Cluster grows in front of it, and it stays idle indefinitely. Editing the filter or breaking the cluster by hand makes it resume immediately.

**Cause (from reading the code)**
`PartSmartAnnihilationPlane.tickingRequest()` returns `SLEEP` when `!isActive()`. AE2's `AnnihilationPlanePart` wakes itself up again when its node comes back ([AnnihilationPlanePart.java#L287-L294](https://github.com/AppliedEnergistics/Applied-Energistics-2/blob/neoforge/v19.2.18/src/main/java/appeng/parts/automation/AnnihilationPlanePart.java#L287-L294)):

```java
@Override
protected void onMainNodeStateChanged(IGridNodeListener.State reason) {
    super.onMainNodeStateChanged(reason);
    if (getMainNode().hasGridBooted()) {
        this.refresh();
    }
}
```

`PartSmartAnnihilationPlane` has no such override, and `UpgradeablePart`/`AEBasePart` only update client flags there. So if the plane ticks while it has no power or channel, it sleeps until `onNeighborChanged`/`onUpdateShape` fires or the filter/upgrades change (`updateFilter()` → `refresh()`). With buds this ends in the stuck state: the bud keeps growing while the plane sleeps, and once it's a full cluster nothing in front changes anymore.

**Expected repro (derived from the code)**
1. Network powered only by an Energy Acceptor, with a Smart Annihilation Plane on it.
2. Cut the power until the network is unpowered.
3. Place a block (e.g. stone) in front of the plane.
4. Restore power. AE2's normal Annihilation Plane breaks the block right away; the Smart plane leaves it until the block changes or the filter is edited.

**Suggested fix**
Add the same `onMainNodeStateChanged` override to `PartSmartAnnihilationPlane`.

**Minor, same class:** `onSettingChanged()` only calls `markForSave()`, but the fuzzy mode is only read in `updateFilter()`. So changing Fuzzy Mode in the GUI has no effect until the filter or upgrades change. Calling `updateFilter()` in `onSettingChanged()` would fix that.

[comment by GlodBlock (owner)]
